inspiration.source_location: Set-operator regression queries over foreign tables (lines 100-116): UNION ALL across two tables, INTERSECT and INTERSECT ALL on filtered operands (WHERE c1 >= 800 / c1 >= 400), EXCEPT and EXCEPT ALL on filtered operands (WHERE c1 > 900), each with an ORDER BY over the whole set
inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL-oriented regression suite exercises the full set-operator family against duplicate-bearing rows and filtered operands: distinct UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT drop duplicates, while the ALL quantifiers keep multiset multiplicity (EXCEPT ALL cancels one matching row at a time, INTERSECT ALL keeps the minimum multiplicity), and a final ORDER BY sorts the combined result.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original access-grant audit scenario (grant_log/revoke_log/audit_snapshot with no primary key so re-grants keep duplicate rows). The set-operator syntax is already standard on MariaDB 10.11.7 and runs unchanged; WHERE-filtered operands become explicit table filters; a NULL resource (the default resource) is added so NULL-equality dedupe and NULLS-FIRST ascending ordering inside the set result are observed; a UNION-then-EXCEPT chain tests same-precedence left-to-right grouping, where the two possible groupings return different row counts on this data.

fixture_notes: grant_log carries re-grant duplicates (ada/billing x2, grace/reports x2) so EXCEPT ALL and INTERSECT ALL produce different results from their distinct forms; revoke_log cancels one occurrence of four granted rows and none of the NULL grants; audit_snapshot duplicates grace/reports so INTERSECT ALL emits it twice while INTERSECT emits it once; ada's NULL grant survives every difference; the UNION-EXCEPT chain distinguishes (audit UNION grant) EXCEPT revoke from audit UNION (grant EXCEPT revoke).
determinism_notes: Every result is ordered by (user, resource) with NULLs first under ascending order; the only repeated rows in any result are byte-identical, so intra-tie order is unobservable. No clocks, randomness, or concurrency.
setup: CREATE TABLE grant_log (id INT NOT NULL, user VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, resource VARCHAR(16) NULL)
CREATE TABLE revoke_log (id INT NOT NULL, user VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, resource VARCHAR(16) NULL)
CREATE TABLE audit_snapshot (id INT NOT NULL, user VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, resource VARCHAR(16) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log EXCEPT SELECT user, resource FROM revoke_log ORDER BY user, resource
SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log EXCEPT ALL SELECT user, resource FROM revoke_log ORDER BY user, resource
SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log INTERSECT ALL SELECT user, resource FROM audit_snapshot ORDER BY user, resource
SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log INTERSECT SELECT user, resource FROM audit_snapshot ORDER BY user, resource
SELECT user, resource FROM audit_snapshot UNION SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log EXCEPT SELECT user, resource FROM revoke_log ORDER BY user, resource
SELECT user, resource FROM grant_log UNION ALL SELECT user, resource FROM audit_snapshot ORDER BY user, resource
